newsitem.title: JAPAN: ADNOC naphtha bid at $19-$20 premiums -- traders.
newsitem.headline: ADNOC naphtha bid at $19-$20 premiums -- traders.

text.p: Asian buyers of Abu Dhabi National Oil Co's (ADNOC) term naphtha have bid $19 to $20 per tonne over the ADNOC formula for term contracts starting in July, traders said on Wednesday.
The levels compare with ADNOC's initial offer price of $22.50 over the formula, and with a $17.00 premium set in May for Saudi Aramco's A-180 for the second half of 1997.
In the current term year ending in June, the buyers -- three Japanese trading houses, one Japanese refiner and one South Korean petrochemical firm -- pay a $6.80 premium.
Traders also said that one of the five potential buyers is likely to have submitted two different prices, $20.00 over the formula for pentane-plus and a $16.00 premium for low sulphur naphtha.

Pentane-plus is paraffinic naphtha favoured among petrochemical manufacturers for its high ethylene yields, while low sulphur naphtha is full-range material used by both refiners and petrochemical firms.
In the oil products market, full-range naphtha is usually priced about $2.00 to $3.00 per tonne lower than paraffinic cargoes, traders said.
For example, Saudi Aramco has set the term price for its full-range Jubail naphtha $2.00 per tonne lower than paraffinic A-180 for the July-December period.
ADNOC has in the past sold both pentane-plus and low sulphur naphtha at the same price.
The five buyers are expected to lift a total of 500,000 to 700,000 tonnes of ADNOC naphtha in the next term year, they added.
